result.summary: Replaces the FreeBSD cross-compilation CI job with a native build and test suite run inside a FreeBSD virtual machine using vmactions/freebsd-vm. Adapts CI environment scripts for FreeBSD native tooling, silences lockf warnings from FreeBSD lsof in the test runner, and integrates a custom HTTPConnection in functional tests to avoid BSD ephemeral port collisions.
result.problem: FreeBSD binaries are only cross-compiled in pull request CI without running unit or functional tests, allowing platform-specific regressions to reach the main branch until detected in nightly builds. Running tests natively on FreeBSD also triggers functional test failures due to ephemeral port collisions and lsof lockf warnings on stderr.
evidence: PR description: "We currently cross-compile BSD binaries without testing them in this repository. Running tests before merge should help catch platform-specific regressions that would otherwise first appear in nightly builds."

Commit a2c3b1e27f: "FreeBSD and OpenBSD allocate ephemeral ports from ranges that overlap the functional framework's fixed test ports. An outgoing localhost connection can therefore select its destination port as its source port and connect to itself. The wrong-RPC-port startup test exposed this on FreeBSD as BadStatusLine: POST / HTTP/1.1"

Commit e29fe9068c: "FreeBSD lsof can emit the following warning during parallel tests: lsof: WARNING -- reading lockf list failed: Cannot allocate memory. The functional test runner treats nonempty stderr as failure even when a test exits successfully."
result.scope_notes: The branch currently includes commit 09347b40f0 marked NOMERGE, which runs 25 BSD trials and disables all other CI jobs to benchmark cache behavior; it must be dropped prior to merge. It also introduces a new third-party GitHub Action dependency (vmactions/freebsd-vm@v1).
result.changed_since_previous: Includes changes from #36916 that subclass HTTPConnection to enforce safe ephemeral port ranges across functional test RPC and HTTP clients, along with accompanying netutil unit tests.
result.card: Replaces the FreeBSD cross-compilation CI job with a native build and full test execution inside a FreeBSD virtual machine using vmactions/freebsd-vm. Currently, BSD targets are only cross-compiled in PR CI without executing tests, allowing platform regressions to go undetected until nightly jobs run. The branch also fixes test framework issues exposed by BSD, silencing lsof stderr warnings and preventing ephemeral port collisions in HTTP clients. Depends on #36916 and contains a temporary trial commit disabling other CI jobs that must be dropped before merging.

risk.why: Flaws would only affect CI execution or test suite behavior on BSD platforms without impacting consensus, node operation, or release binaries.
